goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage) responds to soil texture under a common forcing across the Naches watershed
Validation: compare partitioning-related fluxes/states to observations (CANNOT be met — no in-domain observations provided)
key_processes: snow (relevant but not resolvable under uniform forcing)
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (NOT resolvable as climate driver — see feasibility)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves 1-D water partitioning as a function of soil configuration under a prescribed forcing; appropriate for a soil-control partitioning study across a watershed.

answerable: Soil-texture control on ET / surface runoff / sub-surface drainage partitioning under a common (uniform) forcing
Geographic organization of soil-driven partitioning via stratified placement across the domain

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation/climate control on partitioning (rain-snow transition, snowpack, lapse-driven precip phase) — the scientifically dominant control in a 352–1977 m watershed
not_answerable.why: Framework applies uniform forcing with no elevation downscaling; columns stratified by elevation under one forcing vary by soil, not by climate. Snow/SWE response to elevation cannot be isolated.

not_answerable.aspect: Any observation validation of partitioning fluxes or states
not_answerable.why: observations_available is empty for this domain; there is nothing to compare against in-domain.
not_answerable.needs: observation-dataset ingest (streamflow, SNOTEL SWE, soil moisture)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (soil texture primary; elevation bands as placement/organization axis only, NOT a climate treatment)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Primary axis is 3 dominant soil classes; crossing with 3 elevation bands (used to sample where each soil actually occurs geographically, not as a climate lever) gives 9 cells, with light replication (~2 per cell) = 18 to capture within-cell soil variability. N is not constrained by observations (none exist). Elevation bands do NOT claim a climate effect under uniform forcing.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns where dominant soils occur across the landscape; oversample valley-bottom/riparian soils where drainage and soil-moisture storage differences are largest. Spread remaining columns to span soil classes at mid and upper bands. Downstream expander samples real DEM/soil rasters to instantiate points.
sampling_strategy.replication: ~2 columns per soil×band cell to sample within-class soil heterogeneity.

sampling_plan.reason: High-infiltration coarse substrate in valley bottoms — isolates drainage-dominated partitioning.
Medium-texture valley soils — baseline balanced ET/runoff/drainage response.
Low-permeability valley soils — isolates surface-runoff-dominated partitioning.
Coarse soils at mid band — soil control on drainage where different soils co-occur.
Medium soils at mid band — reference partitioning across landscape position.
Fine soils at mid band — runoff/storage response under common forcing.
Coarse upper-band soils — drainage partitioning at high elevation (climate NOT varied).
Medium upper-band soils — completes soil×band coverage.
Fine upper-band soils — bounds runoff-dominated end member across landscape.

validation_design.observation_source: none provided in-domain (USGS gauge / SNOTEL would be needed)
validation_design.comparison: none possible — flagged as GAP; could only be done as analog-site process validation if an external source is ingested

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: common baseline forcing (single representative period from 1980–2018), native gridded soil per column

requires_capabilities.why: To represent lapse-driven temperature/precip and precip-phase across 352–1977 m
requires_capabilities.blocks: Isolating the elevation/climate control on partitioning — the dominant real-world driver

requires_capabilities.why: Rain-snow transition and snowmelt timing govern runoff partitioning here

requires_capabilities.capability: observation-dataset ingest (streamflow, SNOTEL SWE, soil moisture)
gridded soil raster sampling + DEM sampling in expander
requires_capabilities.why: To instantiate stratified soil×elevation placement into real coordinates
requires_capabilities.blocks: Turning this strategy into concrete columns

assumptions: User request to output 20 raw coordinates + full configs is declined: coordinates come from the downstream expander and configs from the validated configurator; producing them here would fabricate data and risk invalid configs.
A single representative forcing period from 1980–2018 is applied uniformly to all columns (no downscaling).
Elevation bands are used only to place columns across the landscape, not as a validated climate treatment.
Dominant soil classes (coarse/loam/fine) are assumed present and will be confirmed by the soil-raster expander.
open_questions: Can any observation source (USGS gauge on the Naches, nearby SNOTEL SWE) be ingested to enable validation?
Is elevation-downscaled forcing a priority — if so, the elevation mechanism becomes answerable and N/strata should be redesigned around it?
Should exploratory N be reduced (e.g. to 9–12) since there is no observational constraint, rather than scaled toward the requested 20?
